source_proof: TimeSeriesSink.cpp fillTagsColumns sorts key/value tags and injects __name__ before makeTagsBlock computes full ID; tags_deduplication_cache->filterOutWrittenRows is AFTER the sort and id hash. JSON sort order differs but stored Map canonicalization is identical.
method: One Github-hosted Ubuntu24 runner, four fresh stock-O1 servers A0 sorted/B1 shuffled/B2 shuffled/A3 sorted, same series ROW order and exact logical sample values/timestamps; only serialized JSON Map key order changes. SHA-pinned canonical content, RAW UUID v11 outer TimeSeries, three inner targets STOP MERGES, whole process watchdog+worker CPU/IO deltas, global cache event counter deltas, physical TAGS IDs+stored Map fingerprint, full native avg by(project)(avg_over_time(tslab_r23_tag_order_gauge[30m])) 3 warmups+6 measured each phase, QueryFinish CPU/read rows/bytes/peak, A/A drift <=25%; practical CPU threshold 5% or >A/A drift.

querylog_insert_cpu_ms.note: QueryFinish pipeline CPU is not the whole process insert CPU. Do not conflate or claim the ~12% query-log difference as a source CPU saving.

limitations: Only one runner with two phases each mode; 0.5% process CPU delta is below 5% practical threshold and 5.1% A/A drift; do not claim positive speedup.
Client-side pre-sorting does not remove the std::sort cost: TimeSeriesSink injects the __name__ tag at the end of the vector and sorts again.
Entire JSON parsing, canonical tag collection and id hashing remain before cache filter. This is total-write CPU, not exclusive std::sort instruction count.
Stock O1/glibc and 4096 series x24 one-point batches, 20 canonical labels, no natural merges during measured write; production optimized, multi-tenant, high-cardinal 14d not tested.
No CPU profiling stack; input map ordering alone cannot attribute individual parser or sort costs.
